# Tabs

Switches between related panels of content in the same place.

```tsx
import { Tabs } from '@kafka/react'
```

## When to use it

- To split one subject into 2–6 parallel views that the reader compares or picks between.

## When not to

- For steps in a sequence: use Stepper.
- For navigating to other pages: use links or Breadcrumbs.
- When the reader needs to see two panels at once.

## Examples

### Program details

Arrow keys move between tabs and show their panel; Tab goes from the list into the panel.

```tsx
<Tabs
  label="Detalles del programa"
  items={[
    { value: 'resumen', label: 'Resumen', content: <p>Cuatro sábados de lectura y escritura, de 9 a 12 m.</p> },
    { value: 'programa', label: 'Programa', content: <p>Sesión 1: la arquitectura del texto. Sesión 2: el punto de vista.</p> },
    { value: 'precio', label: 'Precio', content: <p>$200.000 COP, con 10 % de descuento para antiguos participantes.</p> },
    { value: 'pronto', label: 'Próximamente', content: <p>No disponible.</p>, disabled: true },
  ]}
/>
```

## Accessibility

- **Pattern:** `tablist` / `tab` / `tabpanel`, with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`.
- **Keyboard:** Left and Right (and Home, End) move and activate; only the selected tab is in the Tab order; Tab then goes into the panel.
- **Target:** each tab is 44 px tall; the selected tab is shown by an underline and bold weight, not by colour alone.

## Content

- Keep tab labels to one or two words.
- Do not hide essential content in a tab the reader may never open.
